<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s).

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ddd64a7564886b7928c91b53f6b9af068ffa9c5d` — the merge of head `955b5e68b76dd756583e009c28b58fc7a56967b7` into base `ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ddd64a7564886b7928c91b53f6b9af068ffa9c5d && git checkout ddd64a7564886b7928c91b53f6b9af068ffa9c5d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c 955b5e68b76dd756583e009c28b58fc7a56967b7 && git checkout -B drift-repro ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c && git merge --no-ff 955b5e68b76dd756583e009c28b58fc7a56967b7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ff04ad811da54166a5d1114fade5a1a6ab99138c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

security#2 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj

The seat adopts the record below, which an isolated reviewer at the contract-review tier rendered on this head. Some passages are replaced with `[detail held by the security seat]`. The security lane's disclosure rule keeps how an unclosed path is reached off public text. Every finding, grade and verdict is unchanged.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3f64f2e53cf1478fccf76dc4de2058e2a8b7bd2f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/agent-ceiling-grant-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/agent-ceiling-grant-refusal.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-start-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/grant-table-write-contract.dogfood.test.ts + read in the cited code, not reviewed: docs/adr/0090-permission-model-v2-concept-convergence.md (D10, D12 as amended), docs/adr/0151-ai-service-account-a-headless-agent-is-a-registered-principal-of-its-own.md (D3), packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/membership-role.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-history-and-publish.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-class-head.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/builtin-positions.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/reserved-identity-names.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/app-default-permission-set.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/idp-group-mapping-admin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/scim-group-projection.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/demo-staff.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/member-role-canonical.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-organization-plugin.ts. Prose faces read for their claims only: .changeset/sec-hardening-agent-ceiling-every-path.md, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx.

Check-runs read on this head (second read): every run that had concluded was `success` or `skipped`. That includes Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, the four Type Check families, every Lint family, Build Docs, Live E2E UI and Test UI. Build Core and Test Core 1/8 to 8/8 were still `in_progress` at the read. No failure was read. The PR is a draft.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`sys_user_permission_set` insert and update: seed writes are now judged** (`judges`, agent-ceiling-grant-refusal.ts:258-260; `onInsert` 263-268, `onUpdate` 271-276).
   - Accept-set narrowed: a write carrying `seedReplay` no longer stands down. **Right.**
   - A seed is a declared fact, and every other validation already runs on it (`SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT`, execution-context.zod.ts:733-739).
   - The flag is read from `input.options.context`, the same place `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts:2095` reads it. The `@objectstack/verify` `seed()` fixture writer carries the same flag and is judged too; consistent.
2. **`sys_user_position` insert, judged for every writer, a system one included** (`onPositionInsert`, 301-308). **Right** as a door. The stated premise is that no system writer of this table has a position of its own to assign. It holds for the writers read: `demo-staff.ts:360-366` and the invitation placement are both failure-isolated, so a refusal costs the position and not the account or the membership.
3. **`sys_user_position` update** (`onPositionUpdate`, 315-326). A write naming a position is judged for every writer; one leaving it as stored is judged for non-system and seed writers only. **Right.** It mirrors the grant table's rule. The one stand-down is a system update that keeps a stored row, and ledger row 23f names it.
4. **Metadata door: one authoring gate for `position`** (`registerPositionAgentCeilingGate`, 335-342; registered at security-plugin-start-hooks.ts:299-302). **Right for the seam's two call sites:**
   - the save door, draft and active (protocol-save.ts:1759-1766);
   - the restore door (protocol-authoring-gate.ts:178-180).

   The seam holds one gate per type (protocol-class-head.ts:168-171), and no other `position` gate exists in the tree, so nothing is displaced. What the seam does not reach is in ④.
5. **`SecurityPlugin` construction now throws** when `fallbackPermissionSet` or `acceptedDefaultPermissionSets` names a ceiling (security-plugin.ts:1604-1609; `refuseAgentCeilingInBaselineOptions`, 363-376). The fallback counts whether it is set directly or derived from an `isDefault` set of `defaultPermissionSets`. Public surface: a constructor that did not throw now does. **Right.** A `null` fallback is not refused.
6. **The existing #30578 refusal's wire shape changes** on every door, the original `sys_user_permission_set` door included (226-233). `constraint` goes from `{ principalKind }` to `{ principalKind, permissionSet }`. The message for that door is byte-identical (default carrier). Additive. **Right**, but the changeset does not state it: nit.
7. **Exports.** `agentCeilingGrantMessage` and `agentCeilingGrantError` gain an optional second parameter. New module exports: `AgentCeilingCarrier`, the carriers, `agentCeilingSetOfPosition` and the two registrars. None is re-exported from the package entry, and no published export moves. **Right.**
8. **Hook binding** goes from two to four under one `packageId`, all replaced together on a second `start()` (395-429). **Right.**
9. **Ledger row 23f** moves its anchor from `#onInsert` / `#onUpdate` to `#judges`, count 1. This matches the code: `judges` is the only reader of `isSystem` in the module. **Right** (Lint · docs & code guards: success).

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is declared identically on the PR body and the changeset.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` is the right kind: a value a metadata author could write in a position's `permissionSets` is now refused at the authoring door.
- `narrowed` takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves. The diff moves `@objectstack/plugin-security` only (the dogfood package publishes nothing), and the changeset declares `minor` on it. **Matches.**
- The BREAKING banner and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`) are present, as on #30578's changeset. Check Changeset: success.

A note on the level, not a level error: #30578 shipped `patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none`. This PR is the first to make the rule a metadata-authoring refusal, and `minor` is the correct consequence.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Open question 1.** The flag: a code-declared position that names a ceiling, changed after it is assigned, gives every holder the ceiling, and stored rows and definitions still give it. Should the rule hold on the read side?

**Confirmed in the tree, and wider than flagged.** The resolver reads every held position's `permissionSets` from the catalog with no principal-kind or ceiling filter (resolve-authz-context.ts:2212-2283, `positionBoundSetNames` 1486-1500). Three further classes sit beside the one the dev measured. All have the same shape: a definition that reaches the catalog without passing the gate, or a holder that never passes the assignment door.
- A position held without an assignment row. `[detail held by the security seat]` (see ④, must-fix 1).
- A position definition stored before this release that later becomes active through a door that does not run the domain gate. `[detail held by the security seat]`
- A channel where both call sites skip the gate by design. `[detail held by the security seat]`

**Disposition: escalated, and split.**
- The choice among A, B and C is a maintainer decision on top of this PR. Option A changes `@objectstack/core`'s read path and takes a held set away from existing principals. That needs its own ruling, changeset and blast radius, and this PR is not the place to make it.
- But the question **does block this PR's claim**: the PR cannot publish the rule as holding on every path while that decision is open (④, must-fix 1).
- For the ruling, a read-only observation: A is the only option that covers all four classes. B covers code declarations, the projection class included, but not stored definitions or pre-release drafts. C leaves the published sentence false.

**Open question 2.** The flag: doors that refuse on the ADR-0090 D12 boundary answer with the boundary's sentence.

**Answered: A, keep.** Not blocking.
- The order is the published one: the delegated-administration gate runs in the security middleware before the hooks.
- #30578's changeset already states that an organization administrator is refused these sets on the organization boundary first, with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`.
- `organizationBoundaryFailure` names the agent ceilings in its by-name sentence (delegated-admin-gate.ts:684-686), so the caller is told why.
- Moving those doors to `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` would change a published status for an authority refusal. That is a separate change with its own declaration, not a defect here.

**Flag: the identity-provider group projection.** It writes grants as `isSystem` without `seedReplay`. It is held only by the boundary's by-name denylist, and no test pins the ceiling names at the mapping door.

**Verified as described, and it holds.**
- One predicate has two readers: the mapping save (idp-group-mapping-admin.ts:384-395) and the admission before each projected grant (scim-group-projection.ts:178-199). So a mapping row that reached the table by another door still grants nothing.
- The denylist names all three ceilings (delegated-admin-gate.ts:378-385).
- The missing pin is real: nothing in this diff fails if a ceiling name leaves that list, and the module note (78-80) and ledger row 23f now rest the hook's stand-down on it. Should-fix 3.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec.** It makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away.
- ADR-0090 D10 gives an agent its ceiling by derivation from consented scopes only. D12 as amended states that an agent ceiling is not a person's set.
- ADR-0151 D3 states that the ceiling sets stay out of the assignment tables for every holder, an AI service account included.
- No text on `main` declares that a position may distribute a ceiling to people. `position.zod.ts` describes by-name distribution in general and says nothing of these three names.
- So each of the four doors refuses something the spec never granted, with #30578's predicate and envelope (`400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, one `fields[]` entry, `invalid_value`, no new code).

Break attempts that did not land:
- **Over-refusal of an ordinary set:** the predicate is an exact match on three imported names (148-151).
- **Over-refusal of an agent principal:** an OAuth agent's ceiling comes from its context and reads no row; an AI service account is refused the same names by ADR-0151 D3's own sentence.
- **A system writer that should be exempt:** none found (① item 2). The one stand-down kept is a system update that leaves the position as stored.
- **Cleanup blocked:** a stored definition can be saved without the set, and a delete is never judged.
- **Envelope drift against #30578:** status, code and field code come from the same builder; only `constraint.permissionSet` is added.

**Must-fix 1. The position path is published as closed and is not.**
- The module note says every other way the platform offers to give a person a set is refused by a door below, and that a definition declared in code is judged at every write of `sys_user_position` (agent-ceiling-grant-refusal.ts:28-44, 294-300). The title and the changeset say the same of every path.
- Read in the tree, a person can hold a position without an assignment row. `[detail held by the security seat]` For such a holder there is no `sys_user_position` write to judge, and the definition is resolved for them by the same catalog read (resolve-authz-context.ts:2212-2283).
- The PR body's acceptance table names `everyone` and the identity positions as the positions held without an assignment, so this class is undisclosed. It joins the classes of open question 1. This review did not run it; it is read from the cited lines.
- Rule (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 10): the claim is kept as narrow as the enforcement. To pass, one of two things holds:
  - the rule is enforced for definitions that do not meet the gate and for holders that do not meet the assignment door (whichever of A or B is ruled); or
  - the module note, the title and the changeset state exactly what the four doors hold and name each residual class, with the decision filed and linked.

  Shipping the universal sentence with the residuals open is the one outcome that cannot pass.

**Should-fix 2. The spec does not say what the consumer now refuses.**
- `position.zod.ts` still tells an author that a holder holds every set named in `permissionSets`.
- A position declared in code naming a ceiling parses and builds clean, and the first signal is a refusal when someone assigns it. That is a metadata-authoring trap.
- The describe on `main` should state the exclusion, with an author-time check or a filed issue for one. That is a spec change on its own face, so it is not required in this diff, but it must not be lost.

**Should-fix 3. No pin holds the ceiling names at the identity-provider mapping door** (③, flag). One test at the save and one at the per-grant admission, each with a positive control, would make the stand-down this module documents fail loudly if the denylist moves.

**Should-fix 4. The changeset's "who moves" omits one effect.** After this release, a non-system update of an existing assignment is refused when the position's stored definition names a ceiling. The refusal lasts until the definition is edited or the row is deleted (`onPositionUpdate`, 322-324). The fix is the one already listed, but an administrator who meets the refusal on an unrelated edit has no line that predicts it.

**Nit 5.** The changeset does not mention the `constraint.permissionSet` addition to the existing `sys_user_permission_set` refusal (① item 6).

**Nit 6.** A boot-time option error is thrown as a `VALIDATION_FAILED` validation failure, while the sibling audience refusal throws a plain configuration error with its own prefix. Both stop the boot; the shapes differ.

**Nit 7.** The authoring seam keeps one gate per type, and a second registration replaces the first without a word (protocol-class-head.ts:168-171). Nothing collides today, but a later `position` gate would silently drop this one.

Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

security#2 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj

The seat adopts the delta record below. The same isolated reviewer rendered it on this head, at the contract-review tier. Its mechanism detail was already withheld by the reviewer.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4ce8e0d642c3b6e78d38f49a1896305e14a36fcf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/agent-ceiling-grant-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/scim-group-projection.test.ts (the delta `3f64f2e53c..4ce8e0d642`, on top of the floor of the record on `3f64f2e53c`, whose code is byte-identical on this head apart from the module note) + read in the cited code, not reviewed: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/idp-group-mapping-admin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/scim-group-projection.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts. Prose faces read for their claims only: .changeset/sec-hardening-agent-ceiling-every-path.md, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx, and the replaced PR title and body.

This is a delta record. It judges two things: whether each finding of the record on `3f64f2e53c` is closed, and whether the narrowed public text is true of the tree. The delta is two commits, `bb91bff1dc` and `4ce8e0d642`. They change a module note, the changeset, one docs row and one test file. No executable line of the four doors moves.

Check-runs read on this head:
- Every run that had concluded was `success` or `skipped`. That includes Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8 and its roll-up, the four Type Check families, every Lint family, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Spec property liveness.
- Two re-runs were `in_progress` at the read: Check Changeset and PR-body guards. Each sat beside a completed `success` of the same name on this head.
- No failure was read. The PR is a draft.

### ① Derived judgments

No accept-set or public-surface change in the delta. The nine judgments of the earlier record stand unchanged, each still **right**.

1. **Module note** (agent-ceiling-grant-refusal.ts:28-48, 82-85, 333-336). It now lists what the doors hold and states what they do not judge. Comment only. **Right.**
2. **Two new pin groups in scim-group-projection.test.ts**, each with a positive control. Tests only. **Right.**
   - The mapping save refuses each of the three ceiling names and stores nothing.
   - The per-grant admission grants nothing for a stored mapping naming one.

   They pin the existing answer at that door (`400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `rule_violation` at `permissionSet`), the answer open question 2 was ruled to keep.
3. **Ledger row 23f:** the anchor and count are unchanged; the prose is narrowed. **Right** (Lint · docs & code guards: success).

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is unchanged on the PR body and the changeset.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and `minor` on `@objectstack/plugin-security` are unchanged and still match.
- The delta adds tests to `@objectstack/plugin-auth` and nothing that publishes from it, so no changeset entry is owed for that package.
- The BREAKING banner and the one ADR-0087 marker are unchanged.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Open question 1.** Unchanged in the tree, as ordered: the read-side rule is not decided in this PR. It no longer blocks, because the published claim is now cut to what the doors hold (④, must-fix 1). It stays escalated as a separate maintainer decision.

**Open question 2.** Answered A, keep, in the earlier record. The new pins hold that answer in place.

**Flag (the identity-provider projection is held by the boundary's by-name denylist, with no pin): closed.** Both readers of the predicate are now pinned for all three names, at the save and at the per-grant admission.

### ④ Design judgment

**Must-fix 1 (the position path was published as closed and was not): closed, by the second branch.** Read against the tree on this head:
- The changeset title, the PR title and the rule paragraph now name four doors and the one refusal, and no longer claim the rule for every path.
- The module note lists exactly the doors the code binds. It no longer offers judging a code-declared definition at assignment as a complete answer.
- The changeset, the module note, row 23f and the PR body each carry the same sentence for what the doors do not judge, in two classes:
  - a position held without an assignment row;
  - a definition that reaches the catalog without passing the metadata door.

  Both classes are true of the tree, and together they cover every residual the earlier record named [detail held by the security seat].
- The PR body's acceptance table now carries that row, and the row the earlier record found incomplete is gone.

The narrowing judgment itself is unchanged: the four doors make the spec's own refusal real and take no declared capability away.

**Rule-level check on the public text: holds.** No role token, channel or door for a residual is named in the delta's added lines, the two commit messages, or the replaced title and body. The two classes are stated as rules only.

**Should-fix 2 (the spec does not say what the consumer refuses): open, deferred by the seat to a follow-up.** It is not required in this diff, as the earlier record said. It is an authoring trap until it lands, so the follow-up must exist and be linked before this is forgotten.

**Should-fix 3 (no pin at the identity-provider mapping door): closed** (③).

**Should-fix 4 (the who-moves line): closed.** The changeset now states that a non-system update of an existing assignment whose position's stored definition names a ceiling is refused until the definition is edited or the row is deleted. That matches `onPositionUpdate`.

**Nit 5 (the `constraint` addition): closed.** The changeset and the PR body state it, and say that the message is unchanged.

**Nits 6 and 7: accepted deviations by the seat.** Recorded; no effect on the verdict.

New on this head, none blocking:

**Should-fix 8. One word in the residual sentence.** The second class reads "without passing the metadata door". The precise rule is "without passing the metadata door's gate", because the gate does not run on every write that goes through that door [detail held by the security seat]. The sentence as written is true for the classes it was written for, and slightly short of one. A one-word change in the four places the sentence appears closes it, and it can ride with the read-side ruling.

**Nit 9. The pointer for the open decision.** The module note and row 23f point at #32004, which is the seat's own card and not a decision record. That is acceptable in a no-card lane. When the read-side ruling lands, both texts need the ruling's reference in its place. The changeset sentence "a separate decision with the maintainer" will then be stale in the shipped CHANGELOG, as any dated sentence is.

**Nit 10.** The who-moves line says "a non-system update"; a seed update of such a row is judged the same way. Too small to hold anything.

No must-fix stands on this head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `955b5e68b76dd756583e009c28b58fc7a56967b7`
